# Testament of Simeon — 2
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Simeon was the fighter — the hard one. His confession isn't about lust like Reuben's. It's about jealousy. The kind that eats you alive.

**1** He was 120 years old. The same year Joseph died, Simeon gathered his sons and spoke.

**2** He told them: I am going to tell you what I have in my heart.

**3** I was Jacob's second son. My mother Leah named me Simeon because God heard her prayer. **4** I grew up strong — I never flinched from anything, never feared anything. My heart was like stone. My gut had no softness in it. That was the gift I had been given: physical courage, iron will.

**5** But that iron will became the thing that nearly destroyed me.

**6** I was jealous of Joseph. Our father loved him more than any of us, and I hated it. **7** And the prince of deceit — the spirit of jealousy — got inside my mind and blinded me. I stopped seeing Joseph as my brother. I stopped caring about Jacob my father. **8** I wanted to kill him.

**9** But God sent an angel and pulled Joseph out of my hands.

**10** Here's what actually happened: I had gone to Shechem for ointment, Reuben had gone to Dothan — and in our absence Judah sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites. **11** When Reuben found out, he was devastated. He had wanted to return Joseph to our father. **12** Even I hadn't wanted him sold — I'd wanted him kept. I'd been guarding him for seven days. But Judah acted while I was away.

**13** For a long time after that, I grieved — not publicly, but inside. Jacob searched and searched. Leah wept. Everyone mourned. **14** And I sat there with my heart hardened by jealousy, not joining the grief, because some part of me still didn't want to feel it.

**15** Two years later, I heard Joseph had been sold into Egypt. And that broke through. I wept. I mourned before God. The shame finally hit me — I had helped put my brother on the road to slavery.

**16** Now listen, sons. Jealousy is a tyrant. It controls everything — it won't let you eat, won't let you drink, won't let you do anything good. **17** It only ever wants one thing: to destroy the person you envy. And while the person you envy is thriving, you are wasting away. **18** The Lord saw what I was plotting against Joseph, and he weakened my hands and feet for two years. I was sick. I couldn't move normally. **19** I knew it was from God. I repented and prayed with everything I had, asking him to remove this plague of jealousy from me. **20** He showed me clearly: this happened because of what I had done to Joseph. And then he healed me.

**21** So hear this: love each other. Drive out jealousy. That spirit makes a person savage. It destroys the body. It turns the mind into a battlefield. It leads to bloodshed. It shuts down your ability to think clearly or act justly.

**22** Even Judah — our most merciful brother — would have freed Joseph from the plot if Simeon's jealousy hadn't dominated the situation. Think about that.

**23** Love your brothers. Honor Levi and Judah. Don't look down on those two. Because from them comes your salvation. **24** God will raise up from Levi a High Priest, and from Judah a King — God and man together — who will save all humanity and all Israel.

**25** And look at Joseph himself. He had God's Spirit in him. He was compassionate and merciful. He never held what we did against us. He loved us the whole time — even more than his own sons. He gave us wealth, cattle, grain. **26** After everything we did to him, he loved us back.

**27** Do the same, my sons. Love each other. Remove envy from your hearts. Love in action, in word, in the deepest desires of your soul.

**28** After this he died, and his sons buried him in Hebron with his fathers. He was 120 years old.

---
*End of Testament of Simeon*
